reference_plate.objective: Read a finite section of |ζ(σ+it)| and locate the critical line among neighboring samples.
reference_plate.equation: Euler–Maclaurin expansion with N=96 through B6
reference_plate.domain: 27 real parts from 0 to 1, 169 imaginary parts from 8 to 32

split-gram-phases.objective: Recognize when one of the two split factors makes a Hermitian denominator noninvertible, and find phases which work in both factors.
split-gram-phases.numerical_method: Exact arithmetic in the two residue fields at 5 for every ordered pair of residues. Four norm-one phases are tested in each of 25 settings.

marked-ideal-weight.objective: Recover the reciprocal ideal-norm power from two covolumes and observe the cancellation of the quotient-lattice scale.
marked-ideal-weight.numerical_method: Exact rational areas for Gaussian coordinate lines, multiplied at three ranks, four ideal generators and three quotient scales.

progression-difference.objective: Read the exact signed contribution of each integer to the scaled endpoint difference and locate the excess over the sharp prime-power sum.
progression-difference.numerical_method: Enumerate all integers through u at twelve cutoff, step and character settings. Use exact rational weights and symbolic multiples of prime logarithms, with an approximate scaled total rounded to four decimal places.

minimum-scale.objective: Compare the guaranteed positive contribution in a primal direction with the exact zero in the chosen test direction for the dual estimate.
minimum-scale.numerical_method: Exact integer enumeration of points a²+b²<4d in Gaussian coordinates, with a²+b²≤d for full weight. The sum of full-weight squared lengths supplies a numerator bound and the number of candidates bounds Z. The displayed fractional lower bound is reduced exactly.

kernel-order.objective: Evaluate the same paired kernel in the two integration orders, identify the conjugated input, and bound the omitted terms before cancellation.
kernel-order.numerical_method: Exact Gaussian-integer partial sums with powers of two as denominators. A parity sum over the two source coordinates is compared with the pairing on the two-point target. The infinite absolute tail is bounded by the complement of the finite square in a convergent product of positive series.

central-period.objective: Compare the period on a full unit cycle with the integral on a movable open arc, including open arcs where cancellation gives equality at particular basepoints.
central-period.numerical_method: The sine difference in the antiderivative is evaluated exactly at eighth-turn endpoints and the result is also rounded to four places when irrational. The solid coefficient curve is drawn through 97 samples.

rank-grid.objective: See how the nine independently chosen entries of a four-by-four array determine every value when all coordinate sums vanish.
rank-grid.numerical_method: Exact products of signed indicator differences at two coordinates of one free orbit for T=5. The two selectors move the basis vector through all nine positions.

euler.objective: See the residue-degree substitution and the effect of two split primes versus one inert prime in the same unramified quotient.
euler.numerical_method: Real powers in binary64, finite products evaluated algebraically. Four base residue sizes and 0.5 ≤ s ≤ 4. A rank-(1,8) algebraic illustration with trivial parameters.

marks.objective: Use the location of the exceptional twists to select one entire multiplicative window.
marks.numerical_method: Selection in base-two logarithmic coordinates with exact dyadic endpoints. The 289 ordered input pairs at exponents 0 through 16 are compared with their forbidden intervals.

floor-sum.objective: Compare the signed floor sum with the special value and examine the unit hypothesis.
floor-sum.numerical_method: Exact integer arithmetic for all units modulo 5, 25 or 125, multipliers 2, 3 and 4, trivial primitive character and k = 2.

jacobi-primes.objective: Lift a cubic character at a chosen split prime, then test the same Jacobi sum and its partner at both primes above p.
jacobi-primes.numerical_method: Count products in {1,ω,ω²} at p = 7, 13 and 19 using the defining power congruence. Reduce in the integral basis (1,ω), multiply the conjugates and evaluate at both roots. All computations are exact. Independent tests enumerate powers of a primitive generator for all six settings.

split-endpoint.objective: Count intermediate lattices above a fixed rank-two endpoint and see how the split Euler factor removes their multiplicity.
split-endpoint.numerical_method: At residue size 2, 3, 4 or 5, compare the coefficient recurrence with Hermite counts for every excess length through 6. Apply the quadratic correction by convolution. The largest uncorrected coefficient is 19531.

gram-pair.objective: Distinguish the diagonal isometry error from overlap between words and see which errors survive an isometric column restriction.
gram-pair.numerical_method: Two normalized two-column maps in real four-space. Compute squared Hilbert–Schmidt sums for both words and their cross block on the full spaces and on the selected coordinate lines. All 18 settings are independently tested by taking inner products of the original scaled columns.

prism.objective: Recover the weight power and the scalar gluing index from the actual alternating prism.
prism.numerical_method: Enumerate all 5ᵉ cyclic words and every insertion in F₁₁× at twist one or two. Products of integer carries and logarithmic indices are reduced modulo five.

satake-average.objective: See how twelve right-K cosets with three induced weights determine the zonal value on one entire double class. Reciprocal parameters can give different weights and the same mean.
satake-average.numerical_method: For the selected exact rational α, calculate nine copies of α/3, two of 1 and one of 3/α. Sum in rational arithmetic and divide by twelve. Floating point is used only for chart coordinates. The six-setting test independently filters the rank-two matrix representatives by their minimum entry valuation.

inert-length.objective: Read a lattice length from the two surviving rows of 3G and see how cancellation changes it even with all entry valuations fixed.
inert-length.numerical_method: For s ∈ {1,2} and t ∈ {0,1,2}, reduce the entries in 𝔽₃[i]/(i²+1). Subtract s times row 3 from row 1, count the pivots, and take nine to that power to find the quotient size. The independent test enumerates every residue-field row combination of the scaled matrix.

inert-cell.objective: Follow the two independent residue sizes through the row count, the corner count, and the number of cosets of one exact length.
inert-cell.numerical_method: With middle rank one and standard middle lattice, evaluate the exact ball counts, then difference successive cumulative counts. The smallest shell starts at length |a|.

flag-average.objective: Compare the distribution of signed line averages for three point configurations and recover the incidence norm on the mean-zero subspace.
flag-average.numerical_method: Enumerate every normalized homogeneous line over the four displayed finite fields. Count by signed sum and use integer arithmetic for both squared norms. The approximate ratio is rounded to four significant digits.

mobius-product.objective: Separate cancellation over the full divisor set from the coefficient that remains after the two length restrictions.

shear-rounding.objective: Read the Schur-complement coordinate correction as a choice of lattice point in a Gaussian basis.
shear-rounding.numerical_method: Round coordinates in fifths, compute both exact quadratic-form distances in units of 1/25 and display their physical positions in the complex plane.

fourier-rank.objective: Observe the loss from retaining only full-rank Fourier frequencies in a finite model of the comparison.
fourier-rank.numerical_method: Enumerate the three independent matrix entries and count all trace phases modulo 3 for each of the 27 frequencies. Character orthogonality reduces their averages exactly.

height-grid.objective: Distinguish the number of grid candidates for one height label from the separate multiplicity of rational classes per centre.
height-grid.numerical_method: Exact counts of integer numerators at all four ordered depths in a two-coordinate, one-real-place grid with R=1. Compare their product to the independent uniform power bound.

trace-cycles.objective: Distinguish one trace around a cycle from a product of traces, and read off how place and block repetition affect a contraction.
trace-cycles.numerical_method: Explicit sums of diagonal matrix entries for the identity and of transposed pairs of entries for the swap, across all selected blocks and supports.

hermitian-density.objective: Relate an unramified Whittaker factor to an explicit count of Hermitian frames at an inert place, and see how congruence lifting preserves the normalized density.
hermitian-density.numerical_method: Enumerate all unit vectors and their ordered orthogonal pairs over the nine-element residue field. At each higher level use the smooth fibre multiplicity 3^(2mn−n²). Compare the result to the Euler polynomial at the special point.

orbit-weights.objective: Distinguish matrix labels and distinct orbit points when normalizing a compactly supported arithmetic partition.
orbit-weights.numerical_method: Two Gram matrices of rank two over ℤ[ω] have 72 preimages each. Direct enumeration of short integer columns checks both multiplicities. Divide each raw weight by the sum over all labels.

genus-mass.objective: See the normalized mass survive regrouping by left cosets and double classes.
genus-mass.numerical_method: Enumerate S₃ and form left and double classes using multiplication.

split-graph.objective: Compute when a selected integral zero-cycle admits an edge filling.
split-graph.numerical_method: Enumerate all pairs over the binary field, form the compatibility graph and count its connected components.

localization-kernel.objective: See which finite-level kernel classes lift to the kernel of an integral localization map.
localization-kernel.numerical_method: Enumerate multiplication by three from ℤ/27 to ℤ/9 and its reductions, computing the two kernels and the cokernel order at each depth.

whittaker-cutoff.objective: Compare a sharp Fourier cutoff with the value obtained by analytic continuation at a nonsingular real target.
whittaker-cutoff.numerical_method: In a rank-one indefinite Gaussian example use explicit Fourier transforms for w=0,1, a sine primitive for w=−1 and composite Simpson quadrature for the integrable cutoff curves.

inertia-orbits.objective: Follow the number of cyclotomic primes above 3 and 7 through levels of conductor 4 to 64.
inertia-orbits.numerical_method: Enumerate the disjoint Frobenius orbits on units modulo 2ᵗ by repeated multiplication.

quadratic-character.objective: See how an injection counts characters even when an invariant character has no extension with the given restrictions.
quadratic-character.numerical_method: Compute the four encoded characters of the index-two subgroup of the semidirect product of the binary plane by the cyclic group of order four.

one-vector-density.objective: Separate primitive vectors from vectors divisible by 3 and read the change of fibre density when the lattice is dilated.
one-vector-density.numerical_method: Exact stratification by the common power of 3 in three Gaussian coordinates. Compare all displayed densities with direct convolution of six rational square counts modulo two consecutive powers of 3.

binary-lattice-limit.objective: Compare the exact normalized count in one binary Hermitian lattice box with its limiting volume.
binary-lattice-limit.numerical_method: The four one-coordinate tents factor. For each scale the counts of pairs with fixed difference modulo 3 give an exact rational answer. A separate calculation sums the tent weights directly.

stickelberger-fibres.objective: See how holding the source level fixed while changing the projection can reveal a nonzero group-ring element.
stickelberger-fibres.numerical_method: Compute the character-weighted integral half-sum with c=13, project onto the pairs of residues modulo ℓᵈ and reduce each integer coefficient modulo ℓ. Two prime characteristics, two source depths and two projection depths give eight exact settings.

primitive-hyperplanes.objective: Count marked hyperplanes by normal lines and by inverse stabilizer orders at one Gaussian lattice.
primitive-hyperplanes.numerical_method: Direct Gaussian coordinate enumeration for squared norm one through four, then common unit identification. For each coordinate pattern the projective orbit size and stabilizer order are related by the lattice automorphism order 384.

dyadic-unit-signs.objective: Calculate the signs of one explicit real cyclotomic unit and its translates, and see the signature index they bound.
dyadic-unit-signs.numerical_method: Evaluate the floor parity at four unit pairs modulo 24 and add the common bit from −1. All 16 parameter choices can be checked separately by the signs of real sine quotients.

minor-shells.objective: Count possible entries of one nonzero Gaussian minor by size, then compare the total cubic weight with a summable upper bound.
minor-shells.numerical_method: Enumerate integer points in each half-open annulus. Sum inverse cubes of their moduli and compare with the exact count times the inverse cube of the inner radius. An independent test enumerates squared norms and uses the multiplicities of signs and coordinate swaps.

cusp-trace-mass.objective: Distinguish the volume of a region from the trace carried there by an orthogonal projector.
cusp-trace-mass.numerical_method: Normalize a two-point function for three measures and three profiles. Multiply each diagonal value by its measure. The test constructs the symmetric projection matrix in an orthonormal coordinate basis and checks idempotence, trace and local contributions.

flag-layer-exponents.objective: Identify the block pairs that contribute each layer of the determinant and recover the unipotent volume factor after taking a square root.
flag-layer-exponents.numerical_method: Sum integer dyadic exponents by block separation, including zero-rank middle blocks. For all 27 settings compare the square root with the independent closed product in the original rank jumps and sizes.

central-rounding.objective: See the effect of rounding half the central target before subtracting the adjoint and compare with the nearest integral central element.
central-rounding.numerical_method: Enumerate quarter-integral targets for the Gaussian hyperbolic plane. Compare the subtract-adjoint construction with enumerated integral skew-adjoint candidates.

convex-nerve-cut.objective: Compare the faces on two closed halves with those on their common slice, including an endpoint shared by a pair of intervals.
convex-nerve-cut.numerical_method: Intersect three intervals and their pairwise intersections with each region. All nine half-step cuts have exact binary representations.

cartan-power.objective: Follow the log of the upper bound for one coefficient as the signed-unitary block grows.
cartan-power.numerical_method: The restricted two-plane exponential has singular values exp(s), exp(−s), 1, 1. Both quantitative bounds are evaluated in logarithms.

parabolic-shell.objective: Compare the mass of a scalar shell with that of a left translate of a product box.
parabolic-shell.numerical_method: Evaluate each coordinate dilation and the reciprocal density at exact dyadic time steps in eighteen settings.

rational-line-orbit.objective: Distinguish rational transport of a line from its intersection with a fixed lattice.
rational-line-orbit.numerical_method: Four rational unit vectors are compared in the Euclidean plane. Coprime integer coordinates give the integral generator on each line. Squared lengths and indices are computed exactly.

gluing-residues.objective: Recover the two fractional coordinates of an integral vector and identify their common gluing class.
gluing-residues.numerical_method: Integer numerators and a common denominator give the two projection coefficients and their residues in [0,1). The rank-one quotient has one generator over the full number ring. The figure counts all classes on the rational integer slice.

regular-unit-shift.objective: Test when a unit lowering produces a regular model and recover its differential eigenvalue.
regular-unit-shift.numerical_method: Exact signed integer weights in U(2,1) give a strict-order test. The group gap holds for all settings.

hyperplane-mass-stratum.objective: Track the maximal-lattice index and local defects for two planes at the same discriminant order.
hyperplane-mass-stratum.numerical_method: Three primes split in the real quadratic subfield and remain inert at both places in the CM extension. Gram entries, indices, discriminant orders and normalized bounds are computed with integers.

casimir-cutoff.objective: Follow the threshold direction through the positive and negative parts and see where the surviving trial vector lies in the cut.
casimir-cutoff.numerical_method: Compute the diagonal multipliers as reduced fractions and use the squared coordinates of the trial vector to evaluate both normalized expectations.

galois-character-peeling.objective: Distinguish an eigenvector at one group element from a line that transforms by a given character on the entire group.
galois-character-peeling.numerical_method: Sign changes give exact coordinates on two summands of a representation of the four group elements. All four are checked to count which transformations carry the candidate according to the chosen character.

frobenius-good-places.objective: Find another good place with the same inverse Frobenius after removing the first witness.
frobenius-good-places.numerical_method: Compute square residues modulo each displayed prime, the residue norm of a prime of the biquadratic field and its inverse modulo seven. The finite exclusion removes all primes over 61.

column-degree-defect.objective: See the formal-degree equality and strict inequality by computing evaluation on a finite group.
column-degree-defect.numerical_method: Enumerate all four group elements and average the reproducing function with the selected Haar mass. Subtract the constant projection and integrate its squared residual.

satake-multiplicities.objective: Distinguish annihilation and determinant tests from recovery of multiplicities at a chosen prime.
satake-multiplicities.numerical_method: Enumerate all nonnegative exponent triples of total degree three and multiply their integer roots. Compare candidate and target trace, determinant and multiplicities.

rank-weight-projectors.objective: Resolve the identity into three weight projectors on four coordinates and identify the blocks sharing one commutator eigenvalue.
rank-weight-projectors.numerical_method: Evaluate the three interpolation polynomials on the four integer diagonal entries and add the resulting projectors coordinate by coordinate. Sum the dimensions of the source-to-target matrix blocks with weight difference one.

weight-circle-spectrum.objective: Distinguish the exponents present in a chosen vector from the common upper bound on each of two diagonal circles.
weight-circle-spectrum.numerical_method: For each of the four degree-three monomials, add its circle exponent to that of the inverse determinant. Keep the distinct exponents with nonzero coefficient for each of three vectors, and compare them to the partial sum of the highest weight (2, −1).

hecke-four-point-approximation.objective: Compare witnesses that attain the radius or have strictly smaller error at the half-dimension threshold.
hecke-four-point-approximation.numerical_method: Evaluate the two fourth-order characters and their indicated combination at all four group elements. Subtract each value from one in the Gaussian integers and obtain its squared 2-adic norm from the integer field norm.

polynomial-cut.objective: Compute the change in five-adic precision when keeping only systems satisfying one nonvanishing test.
polynomial-cut.numerical_method: Compute both finite sums exactly and divide a nonzero integer error by powers of five until reaching a unit.

ordinary-line-cancellation.objective: Follow the two families of lifts of one quotient subspace and compare their multiplicities at the final residue point.
ordinary-line-cancellation.numerical_method: Count the graphs and the full preimage, advance their starting points on the three-cycle by the remaining number of steps, and sum the dimension weights separately for even and odd subspaces.

clopen-branch-reduction.objective: Determine when the projector onto one generic branch extends over the integral model and follow the two branches into the fibre at 5.
clopen-branch-reduction.numerical_method: Evaluate the basis 1, X at 0 and d, with d equal to 1 or 5. Test the denominator of the unique interpolating projector and reduce both roots modulo 5.

quadratic-place-restrictions.objective: Distinguish agreement on the quadratic subfield from agreement on the real subfield when choosing the place of the weight test.
quadratic-place-restrictions.numerical_method: For the four primitive eighth roots in the field of 17 elements evaluate the square and the sum with its inverse, and compare both to the fixed type place.
